Suraj DubeyCOO & CTO, Osource Global
26 October 2026
Proof of concept · Tableau to Power BI

Onex tab2pbi POC

21 public Tableau dashboards were converted to Power BI projects with Onex tab2pbi, opened in Power BI Desktop, refreshed and checked page by page. This document shows each converted dashboard as it renders in Power BI, how much of it was automated, and what is left to do by hand.

21 / 21dashboards converted and loading their data
91.5%of 1,120 migration items automated
87.8%of 262 charts and tables built automatically
290,933rows loaded from 38 tables, no load errors
67 hestimated review and rebuild left, ≈3.2 h per dashboard

How the proof of concept was run

1 · ConvertEach workbook (.twbx) converted with Onex tab2pbi, data files supplied with --data-dir. No manual edits.
2 · Open and refreshEach Power BI project opened in Power BI Desktop and refreshed from the source files.
3 · CheckRows per table, load errors and calculation errors read from the model; every page captured once the data had loaded (27 pages).
4 · DeliverProjects saved with their data, so they open showing it; a migration report lists every item with its status.

Automation summary

Every datasource, field, calculation, chart and dashboard object is one migration item. Converted items match Tableau; approximated items are converted automatically with a note on a known difference to review; manual items are marked in place with the original Tableau definition for a rebuild.

Key points not automated

Tableau table calculations · 30 calculations

WINDOW_MAX/AVG, RANK, INDEX and TOTAL depend on how each Tableau view addresses and partitions the data. They are deliberately not guessed: each keeps its formula and a suggested DAX approach. 14 more calculations use functions without a rule yet (SIN, COS, MAKEPOINT) or depend on a table calculation.

Chart types not built yet · 32 charts

Marked in place for a rebuild: circle 9, line 4, heatmap 3, area 3, bar 3, shape 2, pie 2, square 2, automatic (text) 1. Most are circle and radial designs specific to Tableau.

Some dashboard objects · 14 objects

Highlighter cards, download buttons, missing images and filter cards on calculated fields.

Joins on expressions · 4 joins

Joins on calculated keys need a combined key column; the report names the condition.

Visuals to review after conversion

Scatter charts that plot every row (add the ID to Details), parameter references in titles, currency axes with K / M scaling, a year stored as a number in a date column, and map visuals Power BI asks to upgrade to Azure Maps.

Look and feel

Fonts, colours, tooltips and reference lines take Power BI defaults; dashboards are laid out at the Tableau positions and sizes.

Dashboard details

Each screenshot is the converted report page in Power BI Desktop after the data refresh.

Conclusion

Onex tab2pbi converted all 21 Tableau dashboards into working Power BI projects without manual edits: every data source loads (290,933 rows), 91.5% of the migration items are automated and 87.8% of the charts are built automatically, laid out as in Tableau.

  • 16 of 21 dashboards are usable as converted; the rest load all their data and need a few visuals reviewed.
  • The remaining work is known and listed per item: about 67 hours in total, ≈3.2 hours per dashboard, mostly rebuilding Tableau-specific chart types and table calculations.
  • Several of the remaining points (scatter details, title parameters, number-format scaling, Azure Maps, more chart types) are on the Onex tab2pbi roadmap and will move from manual to automated.
  • Credentials are never copied and only the supplied files are read; output is in Microsoft's open PBIP format, ready for Power BI Desktop and Microsoft Fabric.
